ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the diagram is a generator, which after passing through node 1 is connected to the step-up transformer in the middle; after the transformer it goes to node 2, and then from node 2 it is connected through two parallel transmission lines to the right-side node 3/infinite bus, so the line part is a double-circuit parallel structure. Reasoning: When resistance and susceptance are ignored, the steady-state stability limit power is Pmax = Vg * Vinf / Xeq. It is known that Vg = 1.0 p.u., Vinf = 1.0 p.u., and the initial Pmax = 6.25 p.u., so the initial equivalent total reactance Xinitial = 1 / 6.25 = 0.16 p.u. Among this, the transformer reactance is 0.12 p.u., therefore the equivalent reactance after the double-circuit lines are paralleled is 0.16 - 0.12 = 0.04 p.u. The double-circuit lines are two identical lines in parallel, so the reactance of each line is 2 * 0.04 = 0.08 p.u. If one of the circuits is tripped, only one line remains, and the line reactance becomes 0.08 p.u.; the new total reactance Xnew = 0.12 + 0.08 = 0.20 p.u. Therefore the new steady-state stability limit power Pmax,new = 1 / 0.20 = 5 p.u.

method.method_draft: Use the image to identify the network as transformer reactance in series with the equivalent reactance of the double-circuit line. From the text, Vg = 1.0 p.u., Vinf = 1.0 p.u., transformer reactance Xt = 0.12 p.u., and initial Pmax = 6.25 p.u. Thus initial total reactance Xinitial = (1×1)/6.25 = 0.16 p.u. The initial double-line equivalent is Xline_parallel = 0.16 - 0.12 = 0.04 p.u. Since the image/text indicate a double circuit, one individual circuit has reactance 2×0.04 = 0.08 p.u. After one circuit is tripped, the remaining line reactance is 0.08 p.u., so Xnew = 0.12 + 0.08 = 0.20 p.u. Therefore Pmax,new = 1/0.20 = 5 p.u.

planner_metadata.text_role: Use the stated old limit, voltages, transformer reactance, and the tripping condition; no line reactance value is directly given, so infer the line-section contribution from the old limit.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For fixed terminal voltages and negligible resistance/shunt susceptance, stability limit varies inversely with the net transfer reactance: Pmax,new/Pmax,old = Xold/Xnew.
